parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CMS redacts PII automatically on publish. The original is kept only in the owner's private scope; every other surface receives the redacted form.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: CMS behaviour: publish path runs the redaction policy (name, email, phone) before rendering to web or team chat. A redaction notice names what was redacted and which policy did it.

parts.name: assessment
parts.prose: Evidence: redaction operation receipt naming the triggering policy (operation_id, event_hash). Planned: receipt recorded as OSCAL assessment result and anchored on-chain.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every CMS create, edit, and publish action is attributable: who did it, under what capability, and when.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: CMS behaviour: all mutations run through the subsidiary identity's 3tchedFS call files; the bridge checks the exact capability and commits via MutationEngine.

parts.name: assessment
parts.prose: Evidence: receipt chain per action (required_capability, operation_id, event_id, event_hash, outcome). Proven: bridge issues these fields on every admitted call.

links.text: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5, AC family (access control)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: CMS roles compile into capability grants. Requests outside the grants are refused with the exact missing capability; root-level actions need two different human approvals.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: CMS behaviour: profile compiles to grants and budgets; the team-chat adapter holds no grants and never calls plugins directly. Refusals and approval requests render as first-class results.

parts.name: assessment
parts.prose: Evidence: refusal receipt naming the missing capability and rule; approval record (1 of 2, 2 of 2). Proven: bridge refuses with exact capability name. Planned: two-person rule (elevation ticket is single-use today).

links.text: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5, SI-12 (information handling and retention)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Published CMS content carries a retention schedule; expiry archives or deletes on time, automatically.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: CMS behaviour: each publish sets expires_at; the scheduler runs the archive operation. No silent retention.

parts.name: assessment
parts.prose: Evidence: scheduled-operation receipt (operation_id, event_hash) plus the archived artefact reference. Planned.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Published CMS versions are hash-anchored so anyone can verify what was published, by whom, and under what authority, without trusting the agent or operator.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: CMS behaviour: publish hashes the versioned artefact; the Web3 index entry references the authorising receipt (operation_id, event_hash); the Merkle root is anchored on-chain.

parts.name: assessment
parts.prose: Evidence: index entry (schema/index-entry.schema.json) plus on-chain anchor a judge can check. Planned; receipt fields it cites are proven.

metadata.title: Etched 3tched capabilities catalog
metadata.remarks: Draft for the hackathon. Catalogs 3tched capabilities the golden path needs; each control names implementing plugin operations via props and evidence via assessment parts. Schemas here are drafts; promoted ones become sealed 3tched plugins.
